what: Published values of Grossman & Boudaoud (2026) used as references. There is no reference code: the authors' simulation and computation code is 'available at request' (Data Availability, p. 10). This directory also contains derived comparison evidence and native-solver replay frames for the research page, identified below.

paper.license: CC BY 4.0 (Crossref license record; stated on p. 1)

files.paper_values.json: transcribed by hand from the text and the Supplemental Material, with page and equation numbers
files.paper_figures_vector.json: Figs. 7, 8 and 9 are vector graphics in the PDF; their marks and lines were read from the PDF drawing commands by reference/extract_vector_figures.py (PyMuPDF 2.0, Python 3.14), with the axes calibrated on the drawn major tick marks. Precision about 1e-3 of the axis range
files.fig5_simulation_digitized.csv: Fig. 5 (left) is a raster image (1601 x 558 px, extracted with poppler pdfimages 26.09). Simulation markers and error bars digitised by reference/digitize_fig5.py (numpy 2.5.4, Pillow) with axes calibrated on the drawn ticks. Precision about 0.002 in nu and 0.001 in eta. The eta = 0.49 marker is the paper's 'below the plotted range' arrow
files.published_comparison.json: Derived comparison evidence: native strip means from results/stabileo_results.json against fig5_simulation_digitized.csv error bars with 0.003 digitisation allowance; regenerated in target/reference-results/published_comparison.json by tests/published_series.rs
files.replay.json: Native-solver replay frames for the research page, generated by cargo run --release --bin replay; these are Stabileo outputs, not published paper values
